Letter dated May 10, 1972, from the State Clearinghouse Coordinator, Missouri Department of Community Affairs, with an appended letter by the Executive Director, State Water Resources Board.
<u>Comment</u>: The EIS on the proposed legislation is considered too general, and recommends that a separate EIS be prepared on each species o subspecies proposed for addition to the endangered list.
Response: The National Environmental Policy Act requires an Environmental Statement on each legislative action which may have an environmental impact.

A more precise overall statement is not possible because the species which will come under provisions of the Act years in the future are not predictable.

Therefore, the present statement can only be general in its approach.

Comment: The Missouri reply also suggests inclusion of the alternative of no action.
Response: The Environmental Statement has been revised to include the alternative of continuing administration of the program under the present authority (alternative 5).
<u>Comment</u>: The Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife or another Federal agency be required to prepare a complete environmental impact statement for each program proposed to affect an endangered species and that the statement include consideration of the effect of the act as it relates to the human race.
Response: It should be recognized that benefits to endangered species can, in the long run, be interpreted as human benefits in terms of environmental improvement. While there may be some short-term costs to humans, the human benefits will be long-term as well as short-term. We believe the benefit of the action must be judged on the basis of its own merits.
